title.en: Much as I admire the work

can_do: I can grant a strong objection before I answer it.
I can concede a point in full and still turn the argument.
I can tie two changes together so one rises with the other.

ex: The landlord's forbearance kept them in the house a year.
She answered with a forbearance nobody expected.
He wrote with a temperance the subject rarely gets.
The temperance movement began in the 1830s.
She took the news with complete equanimity.
His equanimity in the meeting was remarkable.
He handled the questions with aplomb.
She corrected the minister with some aplomb.
His diffidence cost him the appointment.
There was no diffidence in the second draft.
He signed it without the slightest compunction.
She felt some compunction about the second letter.
He has no scruples about using the file.
Her one scruple was about naming the source.
Nobody demurred when the date was moved.
She demurred, and then signed anyway.
Forty years of concord ended in a week.
The treaty restored concord along the border.
The visit marked a rapprochement between the two ministries.
Rapprochement took a decade and one funeral.
The wording was changed to conciliate the second district.
He made no attempt to conciliate anyone.
An apology mollified the committee.
Nothing said that evening mollified her.
The fund was set up to placate the villages.
He was not to be placated by a letter.
Appeasing one district encouraged the other two.
The concession appeased nobody.
The grant palliates the shortage; it does not end it.
Nothing in the report palliates the failure.
The lecture was abridged for print.
An abridged edition appeared in 1954.
The district ceded the water rights in 1961.
He ceded the point and kept the argument.
The ministry withheld the annex for a year.
She withheld judgement until the second report.

grammar.label: concessive clauses — for all, much as, however + adjective
grammar.form: For all + noun phrase; Much as + clause; However / Whatever + adjective + subject + be
grammar.meaning: grants a point fully and then sets it aside

explanation.en: 'For all its faults, the plan is the only one costed.' 'Much as I admire the work, the method is unsound.' 'However careful the drafting, a gap remains.' Each concedes something real before the turn — which is what makes the turn persuasive. Note the inverted order after 'however + adjective': the adjective comes first, then subject and verb.
explanation.uz: 'For all its faults, the plan is the only one costed.' Har biri burilishdan oldin haqiqiy bir narsani tan oladi — ishonarlilik shundan. 'However + sifat' dan keyin sifat oldinda, so'ng ega va kesim.

grammar.positive_example: Much as the report is admired, nobody has repeated its central experiment.
grammar.negative_example: Much as the report is admired, but nobody has repeated its experiment.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida 'garchi… bo'lsa-da' konstruksiyasi bor, lekin 'but' ni qo'shib yuborish rus tilidagi 'хотя… но' ta'siri.

grammar.label: comparative correlatives and proportional comparison
grammar.form: The + comparative + clause, the + comparative + clause; in proportion as; the more so because
grammar.meaning: ties two changes together so that one tracks the other

explanation.en: 'The longer the delay, the higher the cost.' Both halves need 'the', and both are clauses even when the verb is left out. At C1 the pattern extends: 'the more so because', 'all the more reason to', 'in proportion as the evidence grew'. The trap is the comma — it separates the two halves and is not optional.
explanation.uz: 'The longer the delay, the higher the cost.' Ikkala qismda ham 'the' kerak. C1 darajada kengayadi: 'the more so because', 'all the more reason to'. Vergul majburiy.

grammar.positive_example: The more detail the annex carries, the less anyone reads it.
grammar.negative_example: More detail the annex carries, less anyone reads it.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida 'qancha… shuncha' juftligi bor, shuning uchun ma'no tanish; xato faqat 'the' ni tushirib qoldirishda.

story.title: Much as I admire the work

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The ministry's own survey says the bridge can wait five years.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Start with the argument against me?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Start with the best version of it. If you answer a weak version, every reader who knows the strong one stops trusting you.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Much as the survey is respected, it assumes a level of traffic that ended in 2019.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Good, and no 'but' after it. 'Much as' has already promised the turn.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I keep wanting to put the 'but' in.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Everyone does. Uzbek and Russian both let you mark it twice.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: For all its faults, the survey is still the only count anybody has made.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Concede that as well, and then say what it would cost to make a better one.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The longer we wait, the more the repair costs. That is the whole argument in nine words.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then let it be nine words. The rest of the page is the evidence for it.
